review_candidates.title: Information Manager – Senegal (national applicants only)
review_candidates.description: Senegal Information Manager – Senegal (national applicants only) Organization International NGO Safety Organisation Posted 10 Sep 2026 Closing date 27 Sep 2026 About INSO Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice. INSO West Africa and Lake Chad Basin Since 2013, INSO has supported the humanitarian community across the region and is looking to establish a regional presence for West Africa at the request of the NGO community. This IM position is based in Dakar, Senegal and reports to the Country Director under the technical guidance of the Technology Team at Headquarters. Overall Purpose of Role The primary goal is to establish and lead Information Management across the West Africa and Lake Chad Basin region. You ensure the quality, consistency, security, and effective use of data for countries without dedicated IM support, while managing key systems such as the CHDC, INSO Portal, and INSO App. You provide data-driven insights through dashboards, maps, charts, and analytical products, advise regional teams on data visualization and information management best practices, strengthen staff and partner capacities, and contribute to the continuous improvement of INSO’s global information management tools and standards. Main Responsibilities Team Leadership & Management Provide strong, inclusive, and structured leadership to the Information and GIS teams, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and professional growth. Line-manage team members through regular supervision, performance management, mentoring, and feedback processes Lead recruitment processes, onboarding, and succession planning for the Information Team Identify skills gaps and design capacity-building plans, including technical and soft-skills development Promote staff wellbeing and resilience, ensuring sustainable workloads and effective prioritization Uphold and enforce data protection, confidentiality, and ethical information management practices Conflict & Humanitarian Data Centre (CHDC) Serve as the regional focal point for the CHDC, ensuring consistent application of data management standards and methodology. Maintain the quality, accuracy, and integrity of CHDC data through regular review, validation, and issue resolution. Coordinate with Programme teams and HQ to ensure consistent incident classification, coding, and data governance. Deliver CHDC training and onboarding sessions for staff and external partners as required. Manage and update CHDC reference data, including actors, locations, and other core data sets. Lead data quality improvement initiatives, including historical data reviews, data cleaning, and user access management. INSO Partners Portal (IPP) and Other Platforms Serve as the regional focal point for the INSO Portal and INSO App, promoting their effective and consistent use across the region. Provide and coordinate user support, troubleshooting, and issue escalation to HQ, ensuring a positive user experience. Deliver training and guidance to staff on Portal and App functionalities, workflows, and partner registration processes. Maintain internal procedures, guidance materials, and cross-training to ensure sustainable support capacity within the Information Team. Monitor and improve the quality, accuracy, and completeness of Portal data, including partner and user records. Coordinate partner registration and user access management, while identifying and reporting system issues and improvements to HQ. Strategic Analysis, Visualization, and Decision Support Lead the development of dashboards, maps, charts, and other data visualizations to support regional analysis and reporting. Advise programme teams on effective data visualization approaches and improve the quality and impact of analytical products. Support and mentor Information Team members in producing high-quality visual and analytical outputs. Extract, analyse, and interpret data from CHDC and other sources to generate insights and decision-support products. Develop, maintain, and enhance dashboards and analytical tools to meet operational and strategic needs. Ensure the accuracy, consistency, and compliance of data visualizations with INSO standards, while driving automation and process improvements. Cross-Departmental Coordination Coordinate Information Management activities across the region and provide regular updates on priorities, progress, risks, and challenges. Support the implementation and communication of updates to CHDC, the INSO Portal, and the INSO App. Collaborate with programme and support teams to deliver information management solutions and technical support. Maintain Information Management documentation, resources, and knowledge-sharing platforms. Contribute to communication and outreach initiatives by supporting the collection and management of relevant information and materials. Represent the Information Management function in internal and external engagements when required. Contribution to Global IM Initiatives Contribute to global and regional Information Management coordination, knowledge sharing, and best practice development. Support the implementation and continuous improvement of INSO’s global Information Management systems, tools, and methodologies. Provide operational feedback and recommendations to enhance global IM platforms and processes. Support cross-country Information Management activities and provide temporary coverage when required. Contribute to the onboarding, mentoring, and development of Information Management staff. Foster collaboration between country, regional, and HQ teams to strengthen Information Management capabilities. IT Support Provide first-line IT support to staff and coordinate issue resolution with HQ IT teams. Act as the local IT focal point, supporting IT projects, troubleshooting, and user assistance. Manage SharePoint permissions, structures, and access to ensure secure information management. Support IT onboarding, software access management, and implementation of IT policies and guidelines. Coordinate software license and user account administration with HQ IT. Support IT procurement and technology-related operational needs when required. Requirements Essential 5+ years of experience in data management, data visualisation, or information management. Minimum 2 years of experience managing a team. Experience with Power BI and DAX, or similar BI software (such as Tableau). Proficiency in database management using SQL. Working knowledge of scripting languages such as Python or R Fluency in English and French, both written and verbal. Basic knowledge of GIS software and systems (e.g., using QGIS or ArcGIS). Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information clearly to non-technical audiences. Nice to have Master’s degree or equivalent in Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Management, GIS, or relevant field. Experience working with humanitarian organisations, particularly NGOs operating in complex contexts. Knowledge of or previous professional experience in Myanmar. Experience delivering training or capacity building related to data or information management tools. Core Competencies Attention to details – Ensures accuracy and quality by carefully reviewing data, reports, and processes. Analytical thinking – Interprets complex data with accuracy to support decision-making. Leadership – Guides and develops team members through mentoring, clear direction, and effective delegation. Collaboration – Fosters teamwork and shared goals across diverse groups. Diplomacy – Builds trust and inclusion through empathy and listening. Communication – Conveys information clearly and adapts to the audience. Proactivity – Anticipates issues and suggests practical, forward-thinking solutions. INSO’s Safeguarding Policy INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps. Terms & Conditions National position. 12-month renewable contract. 1 976 000 F CFA per month salary, 2.5 calendar days annual leave per month. How to apply Please Submit Completed Applications To Jobs@wac.ngosafety.org And Reference ‘WCA Information Manager’ In The Subject Line. Applications Should Be In English And Include An updated CV A one-page cover letter detailing why you are interested in working for INSO and how your qualifications align specifically with the competencies required for the role. Please do not send any additional information. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. review_candidates.title: Health Manager
review_candidates.description: Libya Health Manager Organization International Medical Corps Posted 10 Sep 2026 Closing date 19 Sep 2026 Location: Benghazi / Kufra Job Summary The Health Manager is responsible for the effective implementation, technical quality, monitoring and coordination of International Medical Corps' health activities in Libya. The position provides technical and operational oversight to health teams, supports the delivery of quality health services, and contributes to strengthening the capacity of supported health facilities and healthcare workers in accordance with national guidelines, international standards and IMC policies and procedures. The Health Manager works closely with Program, M/E, Pharmacy, Logistics, HR and other relevant departments to ensure effective implementation of health activities and achievement of project objectives and indicators. The Health Manager also represents IMC with health authorities, UN agencies, NGOs and other health partners and supports IMC's role as co-lead of relevant health coordination mechanisms, including the Health/Nutrition Task Force. Main Tasks Tasks include, but are not limited to, the following: Health Program Management and Technical Oversight Provide technical and operational oversight of IMC health activities and ensure their implementation in accordance with approved project objectives, workplans, budgets, national guidelines, international standards and IMC technical guidance. Coordinate and regularly follow up the implementation of health activities across IMC-supported locations and facilities. Ensure the quality and continuity of health services provided or supported by IMC and identify gaps requiring corrective action. Support health facility assessments, identification of priority needs and development of appropriate interventions based on identified gaps. Ensure appropriate patient registration, referral, follow-up and continuity-of-care mechanisms are implemented in supported facilities. Support implementation and monitoring of infection prevention and control, healthcare waste management and other patient-safety measures in supported facilities. Support preparedness and response to disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies in coordination with relevant health authorities and IMC teams. Monitor epidemiological trends and health risks in IMC operational areas and ensure significant changes or alerts are communicated promptly to management and relevant technical teams. Provide technical guidance to health teams and support resolution of operational and clinical issues affecting implementation. Identify staffing, medical supply, equipment and other operational gaps and coordinate with relevant departments to ensure appropriate and timely follow-up. Ensure patient confidentiality, informed consent and protection of patient information in accordance with IMC policies and applicable standards. Team Management and Capacity Strengthening Provide day-to-day management, technical guidance and supportive supervision to health staff under the position's responsibility Ensure adequate staffing and appropriate deployment of health teams according to project and operational needs Work closely with HR and relevant supervisors on recruitment, performance management, staff development and other personnel matters. Identify staff capacity gaps and opportunities for professional development. Support the development and implementation of capacity-building plans for IMC staff and healthcare workers in supported facilities. Coordinate competency-based training, refresher training, on-the-job mentoring and supportive supervision according to identified needs. Ensure training materials and curricula are technically appropriate and aligned with Ministry of Health, WHO, IMC or other recognized technical standards. Coordinate with internal and external technical specialists and training providers where required. Promote effective communication, teamwork, accountability and adherence to IMC values among health staff. Ensure staff under the position's supervision have clear and updated job descriptions, objectives and responsibilities. Medical Commodities and Equipment Oversight Coordinate with Senior Pharmacist, Logistics/Procurement and health teams to forecast medicines, medical supplies and equipment requirements based on project needs, consumption patterns and available resources. Monitor the availability and appropriate use of medicines, medical supplies and equipment within supported activities. Support timely identification and reporting of stock shortages, consumption trends, expired or near-expiry medicines and equipment functionality issues. Ensure medical commodities are appropriately stored, managed and distributed in accordance with IMC procedures and applicable standards. Support monitoring of medical equipment after distribution to ensure appropriate installation, functionality and use. Coordinate with relevant health authorities and facility management regarding medical supply and equipment needs where appropriate. Monitoring, Reporting and Quality Improvement Work closely with M/E and program teams to ensure accurate, timely and complete collection and analysis of health program data. Regularly review health indicators, service utilization, morbidity trends and other relevant data to identify gaps, trends and areas requiring action. Ensure health program achievements and challenges are appropriately reflected in weekly, monthly, quarterly and donor reports as required. Provide technical health inputs to project reports, proposals, assessments, situation reports and other internal and external documents. Contribute to development and revision of project logframes, indicators, workplans and monitoring tools. Participate in project review meetings and use monitoring findings to support continuous improvement of health activities. Document lessons learned, good practices and relevant program experiences to support institutional learning and future program development. Ensure identified quality or performance gaps are followed by clear corrective actions and appropriate follow-up. Health Coordination and External Representation Represent IMC in relevant health coordination forums, technical working groups and meetings with health authorities, UN agencies, NGOs and other stakeholders, as delegated by the Country Director and/or relevant technical leadership. Support IMC's role as co-lead of the Health/Nutrition Task Force, including preparation of meeting agendas, facilitation or co-facilitation of meetings, documentation of key decisions and action points, and follow-up with Task Force members and relevant stakeholders. Maintain regular coordination with relevant Ministry of Health structures, local health authorities, NCDC, health facilities, UN agencies and health partners in IMC operational areas. Support effective information sharing among health partners and contribute to identification and analysis of health needs, service gaps and response priorities. Contribute to health partner/service mapping, joint assessments and analysis of health response coverage and gaps. Contribute to coordinated health preparedness and response planning, including outbreaks, population movements and other public health emergencies. Support coordination between health facilities, referral services, authorities and health partners to strengthen referral pathways and continuity of care. Promote complementarity between IMC activities and interventions implemented by health authorities and other partners and contribute to avoiding duplication of assistance. Ensure key issues, decisions, gaps and action points arising from external coordination meetings are communicated to IMC management and relevant teams and followed up as appropriate. Maintain professional and constructive relationships with government counterparts, communities, UN agencies, NGOs and other stakeholders. Represent IMC's health programming professionally and ensure external communication is consistent with IMC policies, approved positions and program objectives. Assessments, Preparedness and Program Development Participate in health needs assessments and contribute to identification of emerging health needs and program priorities. Provide technical input into development of new health proposals, concept notes and project modifications as requested. Contribute to design of technically appropriate and context-specific health interventions based on assessment findings and identified service gaps. Support development and updating of health emergency preparedness and response plans in coordination with relevant IMC departments and external stakeholders. Contribute to emergency response activities and rapid assessments when required. Support development of practical recommendations based on assessment findings, health data, partner mapping and coordination discussions. Internal Coordination and Compliance Maintain regular coordination with Program, M/E, Pharmacy, Logistics/Procurement, Finance, HR, Security and other relevant departments to ensure effective implementation of health activities. Participate in relevant internal project, program and operational meetings. Ensure health activities comply with IMC policies, technical standards, safeguarding requirements and donor requirements. Promptly escalate significant programmatic, technical, operational or public health concerns to the appropriate management level. Follow IMC security procedures and coordinate movement and field activities in accordance with country security protocols. Perform other duties related to the position as assigned by the supervisor and required to achieve program and country objectives. Qualifications And Skills Medical degree or other relevant advanced health qualification; postgraduate qualification in public health, health management or a related field is an advantage. Relevant professional experience in health program management, preferably in humanitarian, recovery or development settings. Demonstrated experience in supervision and management of multidisciplinary health teams. Experience working with health authorities, healthcare facilities, UN agencies, NGOs and health coordination mechanisms. Experience in health assessments, capacity building, monitoring and reporting. Experience in emergency preparedness, outbreak response and/or health-system strengthening is an advantage. Strong understanding of quality health-service delivery, referral systems, IPC and management of medical commodities. Strong communication, coordination, facilitation and interpersonal skills. Ability to analyze health data and translate findings into programmatic actions and recommendations. Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and coordinate with multiple internal and external stakeholders. Good written and spoken Arabic and English. Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications. Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our Code of Conduct and Ethics and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our Code of Conduct and Ethics , including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships. International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve. As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staffare required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps. Equal Opportunities International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran. How to apply How To Apply Email your CV and cover letter to: Libya-Recruitment@InternationalMedicalCorps.org Deadline for application: September 19 ***,*** 2026 Date Needed: October 1, 2026 Only applicants who are eligible to work in Libya without employer provided sponsorship are eligible for this position. review_candidates.title: Head of Center- Ain Al Remaneh Read
review_candidates.description: Lebanon Head of Center- Ain Al Remaneh Read Organization Amel Association International Posted 10 Sep 2026 Closing date 15 Sep 2026 Amel Association International (Amel) is a Lebanese and non-sectarian NGO created in 1979. Amel works through 27 centers, 6 mobile medical units, 2 mobile education units and 1 protection unit, and for more than 40 years has supported the poorest regions of Lebanon, from Beirut and its South Suburbs to Mount Lebanon, Bekaa and South Lebanon. Amel offers accessible services for all in the following fields: food security, health, education, protection, child protection, gender-based violence, livelihood, promotion and protection of human rights, rural development. Contact Person Name Jocelyne Hassaba Contact Person Position HR Coordinator Contact Person Email jobs@amel.org Description Amel Association International, in partnership with UNHCR, is implementing a Community Development Project aimed at supporting refugees, asylum seekers, and other persons of concern in Beirut. Through this project, Amel provides a range of educational, psychosocial, vocational, IT, and livelihood support services through community centers located in Beirut. The project aims to promote inclusion, participation, protection, skills development, and access to opportunities for refugees and other persons of concern. Duty Station : Ain El Remmaneh, Beirut General Purpose of the Position The Head of Community Center is responsible for the overall management, coordination, and supervision of the Community Center and its activities. The position ensures the effective implementation of project activities at the center level, in accordance with project objectives, donor requirements, Amel Association International's policies and procedures, and relevant UNHCR policies and standards. The Head of Community Center manages and supervises a multidisciplinary team, including social workers, logistics staff, vocational training and IT trainers, livelihood trainers, and other relevant personnel. The position is responsible for ensuring effective coordination, quality implementation, appropriate resource management, staff supervision, financial follow-up, reporting, networking, and representation. Key Duties And Responsibilities Task 1: Management and Coordination of Project Implementation Manage, coordinate, monitor, and assess the implementation of all Community Center activities in accordance with the project agreement, objectives, work plan, and approved standards. Ensure that all activities are implemented in compliance with Amel Association International's policies and procedures, UNHCR priorities and requirements, and the organization's Code of Conduct. Ensure the smooth implementation and coordination of activities across different sectors and promote effective collaboration among team members. Monitor the quality and progress of activities and ensure that project objectives and expected results are achieved. Set implementation priorities and propose modifications, corrective actions, or improvements when necessary to ensure the effectiveness and relevance of activities. Ensure the efficient and appropriate use of available human, financial, and material resources. Encourage and support the active participation of refugees and other persons of concern in the planning, implementation, and evaluation of activities. Promote community participation and support innovative initiatives and ideas developed by refugee and community groups. Ensure that age, gender, diversity, and inclusion principles are mainstreamed throughout all phases of project implementation. Identify challenges, gaps, and emerging needs at the Center level and communicate them promptly to the Programme Coordinator. Ensure proper coordination and planning of all Center activities and maintain an updated activity schedule. Prepare budget and operational requests related to planned activities and ensure appropriate follow-up on their implementation. Ensure proper documentation of project activities, achievements, challenges, and lessons learned. Task 2:Team Management Follow up on staff attendance, working schedules, and compliance with organizational policies and procedures. Monitor staff performance and ensure that activities are delivered according to expected results, job responsibilities, and contractual obligations. Lead regular team meetings and conduct individual meetings with staff members to ensure effective communication, coordination, teamwork, and synergy between activity areas. Provide guidance, technical and operational support to staff to ensure the effective implementation of their responsibilities. Identify staff capacity-building needs and ensure the participation of employees in relevant educational and training opportunities. Promote staff well-being and contribute to maintaining a positive, respectful, inclusive, and supportive working environment. Follow up on staff leave requests and work schedules in coordination with the Programme Coordinator and Human Resources Department. Address staff concerns and workplace challenges in a timely and professional manner. Report violations of organizational policies, procedures, safeguarding principles, or the Code of Conduct and request appropriate investigation and follow-up in accordance with Amel's established procedures. Ensure effective communication and promote a strong team spirit among all employees working at the Center. Task 3: Financial and Resource Management Manage, monitor, and track Center-related expenses in accordance with the approved project budget and Amel's financial policies and procedures. Prepare budget requests, purchase requests, and other required financial and administrative documentation. Ensure proper receipts, supporting documents, and documentation of all expenditures. Follow up on expenditure reconciliation and financial reporting requirements on a monthly basis. Oversee the proper management and documentation of petty cash available at the Center, in accordance with organizational procedures. Ensure that financial resources are used efficiently, transparently, and exclusively for approved project activities. Coordinate with the Finance, Administration, and Logistics Departments to ensure timely processing of financial and operational requirements. Identify the logistical and operational needs of the Center, including equipment, supplies, furniture, IT materials, and other resources required for the proper implementation of activities. Supervise the proper use, maintenance, and organization of Center equipment and materials. Ensure that procurement and resource requests are submitted in a timely manner to avoid interruptions in project activities. Task 4:Reporting, Coordination, Representation, and Networking Prepare and submit timely and accurate monthly progress reports to the Programme Coordinator. Ensure regular reporting on project achievements, challenges, risks, gaps, and recommendations. Contribute to the preparation of narrative reports, activity reports, and other documentation required by Amel Association International and project donors. Maintain effective communication and coordination with Amel Headquarters and relevant internal departments. Liaise and coordinate with relevant NGOs, UN agencies, government institutions, municipalities, and community-based organizations. Develop and maintain professional relationships and networks with relevant stakeholders working in the social, psychosocial, educational, vocational, and livelihood sectors. Represent Amel Association International in relevant coordination meetings, workshops, and events, in coordination with the Programme Coordinator. Coordinate and facilitate internal and external monitoring visits. Receive and accompany visitors from donor agencies, UN agencies, embassies, partners, and other relevant stakeholders. Promote the visibility and positive representation of Amel Association International and its activities. Task 5: Center Development and Quality Assurance Ensure that the Community Center is properly organized, maintained, safe, and welcoming for beneficiaries, staff, and visitors. Supervise the general organization, cleanliness, and appropriate maintenance of the Center. Participate in the preparation and implementation of work plans, activity schedules, and operational procedures. Continuously work to improve the quality, relevance, and accessibility of services provided by the Center. Ensure that project activities are implemented in accordance with relevant quality standards, policies, procedures, and donor requirements. Identify opportunities to improve and develop Center services based on community needs, beneficiary feedback, and project objectives. Support the active participation of the Center in relevant national campaigns, community events, special occasions, and emergency situations when applicable. Participate in relevant internal and external committees, coordination mechanisms, and working groups. Maintain professional confidentiality and ensure the protection of beneficiaries' and staff members' privacy and personal information. Promote accountability, inclusion, non-discrimination, and respect for diversity in all Center activities. Task 6: Safeguarding, Protection, and Occupational Safety Responsibilities Ensure compliance with Amel Association International's safeguarding policies, Code of Conduct, protection principles, and relevant procedures. Promote a safe, respectful, inclusive, and protective environment for all beneficiaries, staff members, volunteers, and visitors. Ensure that safeguarding concerns, incidents, or violations are reported and addressed through the appropriate organizational mechanisms. Maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information in accordance with organizational policies and data protection principles. Ensure compliance with general health, safety, and occupational safety procedures at the Center. Take appropriate measures to ensure a healthy and safe working environment for staff, beneficiaries, and visitors. Identify potential safety and security risks within the Center and report them to the relevant management and administrative departments. Ensure that staff are aware of and comply with relevant safety, security, emergency, and occupational health procedures. Coordinate with relevant stakeholders and authorities when required to address safety, protection, or emergency-related concerns. Adhere to all instructions and guidelines related to occupational health and safety to ensure self-protection and the protection of colleagues and beneficies. Education Degree Details Master's degree in Management, Social Work, International or Humanitarian Affairs, Political Sciences, Community Development, or another relevant field. A Bachelor's degree combined with significant relevant professional experience may be considered. Experience working with an NGO, humanitarian organization, or international organization is highly desirable. Previous experience working with refugees, asylum seekers, vulnerable populations, or community-based projects is an asset. Required Skills And Competencies Strong leadership and team management skills. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Strong organizational, planning, and coordination skills. Ability to work effectively in a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment. Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities and work under pressure. Good financial and budget monitoring skills. Strong reporting and documentation skills. Good computer literacy, including proficiency in Microsoft Office applications. Ability to work independently while maintaining effective teamwork and coordination. Strong sense of responsibility, accountability, and initiative. Commitment to humanitarian principles, safeguarding, inclusion, non-discrimination, and confidentiality. Respect for applicable laws, organizational policies, procedures, and professional standards. Experience 3 to 5 years of relevant professional experience, preferably in project management, community development, humanitarian assistance, or NGO programming. Previous experience in supervising and managing a multidisciplinary team is highly desirable. How to apply Please send your CV to jobs@amel.org ,marked "Head of center" in the subject line. The CV should be in English and to be sent as word or pdf attachments. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Thank you for your interest in joining Amel Association. review_candidates.title: Head Of Experimental Physics
review_candidates.description: Share Head of Experimental Physics Madison, WI Lead the experiments that will define the future of fusion energy. The Head of Experimental Physics will lead Realta Fusion’s experimental program to advance the physics basis for high-field axisymmetric mirror fusion. This role is responsible for setting the strategic direction, execution, and growth of the company’s experimental physics efforts, while remaining technically engaged in key research initiatives. This leader will oversee experimental campaigns on the Wisconsin HTS Axisymmetric Mirror (WHAM) at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, guide the development of advanced plasma diagnostics, and drive the experimental roadmap for Realta’s next-generation device Hammir. The role requires close integration with theory, modeling, and engineering teams to ensure alignment between experimental results and device design. The Head of Experimental Physics will build and lead a high-performing team, establish strong external collaborations with national laboratories and academic institutions, and represent Realta’s experimental program through publications, conferences, and partnerships. Realta Fusion is a rapidly growing start-up developing compact magnetic mirror fusion energy systems to address the biggest challenge of our time –tackling global climate change while ensuring a sufficient energy supply for at least ten billion people on (and off) earth. We are building a team with diverse talents dedicated to making fusion energy a real solution to humanity’s most pressing problem. Responsibilities Define and execute Realta’s experimental physics strategy aligned with the fusion roadmap. Set priorities for experimental campaigns, diagnostics development, and validation efforts across WHAM and Hammir. Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing experimental physics team. review_candidates.title: Senior AI Engineer — Microsoft Foundry Agents
review_candidates.description: Description One of New Zealand's largest banks is building a production, multi-agent AI platform on Microsoft Foundry. Not a proof of concept. Not a chatbot bolted onto a FAQ page. A governed fleet of agents with real identities, real tool access, and real accountability — talking to each other over A2A, grounded in enterprise data. What you'll actually build Conversational and task agents on Foundry Agent Service — hosted agents, prompt agents, and (where the risk case supports it) autonomous patterns. Python and/or C#. Multi-agent orchestration using Microsoft Agent Framework — supervisor/worker, handoff, and Magentic-style patterns. Deciding when an orchestrator earns its complexity and when a single agent with good tools is the better answer. Agent-to-agent (A2A) interoperability — Agent Cards, capability discovery, delegation across agents that don't share a stack or an owner. Both directions: calling remote agents as tools, and exposing agents for others to call. Tool and knowledge layers — MCP servers and clients, Foundry Toolboxes, OpenAPI tools, and grounding via Foundry IQ / Azure AI Search over the bank's own content. Retrieval that actually retrieves the right thing. Agent identity and governance — Entra Agent ID, agent blueprints, Conditional Access for non-human identities, OAuth identity passthrough so an agent acting for a customer can only ever see what that customer can see. Evaluation and observability — groundedness, relevance and safety evals wired into CI; tracing through Application Insights; the ability to answer "why did the agent say that" six months after it said it. Guardrails that hold up to a regulator — content filters, prompt injection defences, PII handling, human-in-the-loop checkpoints on anything that touches money or advice. Channel delivery — surfacing agents into Teams, M365 Copilot, and customer-facing front ends. You will also spend real time with risk, compliance, privacy and architecture teams. In a bank, the engineering is half the job. Being able to explain your design to someone whose job is to say no — and win — is the other half. Why this one is worth your time Genuinely cutting edge. Foundry's agent stack, Agent Framework, A2A v1, Entra Agent ID — most of this shipped or went GA in the last two quarters. You will be among the first people in New Zealand to run it in production, in a bank. Visibility. Executive sponsorship, board-level interest, and a delivery team small enough that your work is identifiable. No hiding, but no anonymity either. Scope to architect, not just implement. The patterns for this don't exist yet in the client's environment. You'll help set them. Requirements Non-negotiable: Strong Python and/or C# / .NET. You write production code, not notebooks. Hands-on with Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Foundry) — Agent Service, model deployments, evaluations. You've shipped something with it, not just watched the Build session. Real experience with agentic architectures: tool calling, function calling, orchestration, memory, state, context engineering. Whether you got there via Microsoft Agent Framework, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, LangGraph or your own harness, we care that you understand the failure modes. MCP in anger — you've built or integrated servers, and you know why tool sprawl kills agent accuracy. Solid Azure platform fundamentals: Entra ID, managed identities, App Service / Container Apps / AKS, Key Vault, private networking and VNet integration, Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions. RAG done properly — chunking, hybrid search, reranking, and the honesty to know when retrieval is the problem and when the model is. Communication. You'll be in front of stakeholders who are senior, sceptical, and time-poor. Strongly preferred: A2A protocol experience — v1.0 spec, Agent Cards, cross-platform delegation. Entra Agent ID and non-human identity governance. Prior work in banking, insurance or another regulated industry — you understand why "it works" isn't the same as "it's approved." Exposure to responsible AI practice: red teaming, adversarial testing, model risk governance, AI evaluation frameworks. Azure Fabric / Databricks / enterprise data platform context. Relevant certifications (AI-102, AZ-204, AZ-305) — useful, not a substitute for shipped work.
